problem_markdown: Among permutations $(x_1,\ldots,x_{2n})$ of $\{1,\ldots,2n\}$, prove more have an adjacent pair with $|x_i-x_{i+1}|=n$ than have none.
solutions_markdown:
Let $E_j$ be the event that $j$ and $j+n$ are adjacent. Treating the pair as a block in either order gives $|E_j|=2(2n-1)!$. For $j\ne k$, treating both pairs as blocks gives $|E_j\cap E_k|=4(2n-2)!$.

The two-term inclusion–exclusion bound gives
$$\left|\bigcup_{j=1}^nE_j\right|\ge2n(2n-1)!-4\binom n2(2n-2)!=2n^2(2n-2)!.$$
This exceeds half of $(2n)!$, because
$$2n^2-n(2n-1)=n>0.$$
Thus the required property holds for a strict majority. The lower bound itself follows pointwise: an object belonging to $r$ events contributes $r-\binom r2\le1$ when $r\ge1$, and zero when $r=0$.
